analysis: Only a Swift test file changed (provider-swift/Tests/ProviderCoreTests/Config/ClusterRuntimeApprovalFactsTests.swift). It ships no production code, so there is no direct change to the attack surface, trust boundaries, or keys, and no threat-model control is weakened by the diff itself. The tests exercise ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts: a v2 canonical schema with pair_serving_grant and parity_qualifications, a strict decoder, and release/candidate selection. The strict decoder rejects unknown, missing, mistyped, and duplicate keys, including escape-spelled ones. Derived-ID length bounds and the grant/qualification validation rules are also covered, along with a golden canonical-bytes check. These tests strengthen verification of the facts consumed by the platform's build-qualification path (A-017, T-054, TB-011). I checked for any weakening of security expectations, such as tests that assert insecure behavior or embed secrets. Fixtures contain only public digests and test hashes, with no credentials. One security-relevant semantic to note: declared models (ClusterPublicModels.declared) get their grant from owner-declared families with an evidence-document digest, regardless of the bundled records (test grantIsTheDeclaredFamilies...). Production-side behavior, namely how the coordinator/platform consumes and validates such declared grants, is outside the supplied evidence and is platform-owned. I treat that as an unverified contract rather than a finding. The T-041 prefix-cache definition is not touched by this diff. The test reads fixture files and the repository evidence document by path, and it uses temporary directories only. No ordering, authorization, or encryption logic appears in this diff. The production source (ClusterRuntimeApprovalFacts, ClusterPublicModels) was not supplied, so test assertions are not verified against the implementation.
